Level: "Al corridoio discendente segue un breve tratto piano (G), della medesima larghezza, ma di altezza maggiore", p. 39. The same sentence gives it the corridor's width, which is why the route lets it take the descending corridor's section; its height is only "greater", so the drawn stretch is lower than the real one, which is a filled hole and said here.

Taken as level. Perring's table in Vyse's Appendix, p. 121, gives "From anteroom to end of the three portcullises, 13 ft 5 in" with no angle and then an angle, 4°, for the passage beyond; Maragioglio and Rinaldi, p. 41, single out that passage (I) as "non è orizzontale, ma inclinato di circa 4°" and say nothing of a slope in (S). Neither says in words that (S) is level, so this is an inference and stays unverified. It is checked by the route: with (S) level the large chamber's floor comes out within a few centimetres of the level Tav. 4 prints for it.

Printed [10.55] on Tav. 4, fig. 2 (Sezione S-N) and fig. 5 (Sezione E-W), dimensioned from the base line down to the floor of the large chamber (B). Square brackets on this plate mark Perring's figures, as its own "lato base [108.05] (105.50)" shows beside the Petrie figure in round ones. Not used to build anything: the route places the chamber from the chain of passages, and this is what its floor is checked against.

Due west: "parte un corridoio discendente (R), diretto verso ovest", p. 43. Petrie, §86, has the same passage descend "westwards" out of the middle of the second chamber's floor. The portcullis and the foot of the incline continue this bearing, and the horizontal passage after them.

No slope is printed for this corridor and neither Petrie nor the Parte VI text states one. Scaled with scripts/plate.py on Tav. 6, fig. 8 ("Sezione αα guardando a nord"), rasterised at 300 dpi clipped to (1300, 1500, 2420, 1960) pt: the dimension line printed "~9.90", drawn parallel to the corridor, from (2875, 1420) to (3625, 1030) gives 27.47 deg with a pixel and drafting sigma of 0.8; a second line parallel to the passage, from (2600, 1325) to (3100, 1075), gives 26.57; the rough rock-cut walls read between 25.4 and 29.1. Sigma covers the walls. Stored negative, descending away from the chamber. Maragioglio and Rinaldi, p. 43, say the corridor was first cut at a lesser slope and later made steeper; this is the steeper, present one. The portcullis slot and the foot of the incline continue it.

Level: "Length of horizontal passage to the apartment of the sarcophagus, 10 ft 0 in", Perring's Table of Dimensions of the Third Pyramid, Vyse vol. II, Appendix, pp. 120 to 122; Maragioglio and Rinaldi, p. 45, call it "un passaggio orizzontale (Z)" too. They add that its floor has a step about 15 cm high a little over 90 cm beyond the portcullis, which the scene does not draw.

"The doorway is 54.52 wide, and one side of it in the plane of the S. wall", §87: the doorway into the crypt, in its east side, starts at the south wall. So the passage (Z) runs in along the crypt's south wall, and the route stands the crypt's south wall half a doorway south of the passage's axis.

A member with a branch.step begins on the member with that step instead of where the one before it ends; see the route in packages/geometry/src/interiors.ts.

The stair opens off step 10, the horizontal passage (Z): "nella parete nord del corridoio (Z) si apre una porta, munita superiormente e ad ovest di una battuta, che dà accesso ad una scaletta in discesa (P)", p. 47, and p. 45 puts that door in the north wall past the cuts made for setting the portcullis. Vyse, p. 85, has the steps "on the opposite side" to a recess in the south side of the passage, and Petrie, section 88, has them "turning out of the passage to the granite chamber".

How far back along the horizontal passage (Z) from its end at the crypt's east wall the middle of the stair's doorway stands. No source prints it. Scaled from Tav. 4, fig. 6 ("Pianta della cripta"), rasterised with scripts/plate.py at 600 dpi clipped to (1430, 1500, 1800, 1780) pt, against the plate's 20 m scale bar (rasterised at 600 dpi clipped to (1460, 1075, 1800, 1110) pt, its ends at pixels 121 and 2496, 0.0084211 m per pixel, which is the sheet's 1:200). No figure on fig. 6 is printed in metres to check the bar against, so the checks are the survey's: the crypt's inside scales 6.459 by 2.535 m against Petrie's 6.599 by 2.633 and the passage (Z) 1.406 m wide against Perring's 1.372, and the largest of those, 3.7 per cent, is taken as the shrinkage. The crypt's inner east face is at pixel x 676 and the doorway in the passage's north wall runs from the stair's west wall at x 897, which is the room's west wall carried down to the passage, to its east wall at x 1017, so its middle is at x 957: from (676, 1438) to (957, 1438), 281 pixels, 2.366 m. Sigma sums the pixel term 0.036 m (3 px at each end), the drafting tolerance 0.100 m (half a millimetre at 1:200) and the shrinkage 0.088 m. The E-W section on the same sheet, fig. 5, draws the doorway as a rectangle in the passage's north wall and gives 2.466 m for the same distance, from (767.5, 700) to (1060.3, 700) on a render clipped to (1420, 1400, 1620, 1520) pt, inside the sigma.

The stair's bearing. No source states it; Vyse says only that the steps open into the southern end of the room. Scaled from Tav. 4, fig. 6 ("Pianta della cripta"), rasterised with scripts/plate.py at 600 dpi clipped to (1430, 1500, 1800, 1780) pt, against the plate's 20 m scale bar (rasterised at 600 dpi clipped to (1460, 1075, 1800, 1110) pt, its ends at pixels 121 and 2496, 0.0084211 m per pixel, which is the sheet's 1:200). No figure on fig. 6 is printed in metres to check the bar against, so the checks are the survey's: the crypt's inside scales 6.459 by 2.535 m against Petrie's 6.599 by 2.633 and the passage (Z) 1.406 m wide against Perring's 1.372, and the largest of those, 3.7 per cent, is taken as the shrinkage. The stair's west wall is the room's west wall carried straight down to the passage (Z), and from (897, 1437) to (1360, 400) it reads 24.1 deg east of the square to the passage, whose north wall is level on the scan to a pixel over 225 pixels, so the passage's due west is the reference. The stair's east wall, from (1017, 1462) to (1097, 1285), reads 24.3 deg. Sigma sums the wall's pixel and drafting term, 0.8 deg, and half a degree for the reference. It is the room's 25 deg within that, so the stair runs along the room.

No source gives the stair a height. Scaled from Tav. 4, fig. 5 ("Sezione E-W"), which draws the stair's doorway (P) as a rectangle in the north wall of the passage (Z): rasterised with scripts/plate.py at 600 dpi clipped to (1420, 1400, 1620, 1520) pt, from the passage floor at (1060, 793) to the doorway's head at (1060, 632), 161 pixels at the plate's 20 m bar (0.0084211 m per pixel), 1.356 m. The section is drawn loosely in height: the crypt's inside scales 2.606 m wide against Petrie's 2.633, but the passage (Z) 1.857 m high against Perring's 2.057, so the shrinkage is taken as 9.7 per cent. Sigma sums the pixel term 0.036 m, the drafting tolerance 0.100 m and that shrinkage, 0.132 m. It is the doorway's height, measured plumb, and the route draws the stair with it square to the stair's slope of 28.4 deg, which gives 0.19 m more headroom measured plumb, inside the sigma.
